equity_bridge.item: Redeemable and other noncontrolling interests at book
equity_bridge.note: FY2026 10-K balance sheet: redeemable NCI 85 + NCI 8

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: organic growth (FY2025 7.7%, FY2026 11.3%), not equity CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR is undefined: stockholders' equity has been negative since FY2013 and stands at $(10.0)bn because of debt-funded special dividends. The house default (equity CAGR) cannot be applied. Revenue CAGRs of ~17% include acquisitions (acquisition growth 8.2% in FY2026) and the post-COVID recovery from a depressed FY2021 base, which also flatters the 5-year EPS and FCF figures.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner series (reported FCF less SBC and dividend-equivalent payments; FY2021 dividend equivalents were not available and are not deducted, slightly overstating the FY2021 base and understating the 5-year CAGR). These are levered FCFs: interest paid rose from $1.16bn (FY2024) to $1.92bn (FY2026) as special dividends, buybacks and acquisitions were debt-funded, which is why reported FCF was flat FY2024-FY2026 (1,880 / 1,816 / 1,913) while EBITDA As Defined grew 33%. Owner and reported FCF CAGRs are close; SBC is ~1.5% of revenue and not growing faster than cash flow.

scenario_narratives.base: Commercial aftermarket (32% of sales, the highest-margin stream) keeps growing high-single-digit on flight hours, an ageing fleet kept in service by OEM delivery shortfalls, and real pricing on sole-source proprietary parts; commercial OEM recovers with Boeing and Airbus rate increases; defense grows mid-single-digit. Organic growth fades from ~7% to 4% over the decade. The FY2026 acquisitions (Simmonds, JPE/VSA, P&I), bought at margins roughly half the group's, are worked up toward group levels as every prior TransDigm acquisition has been, taking EBITDA As Defined margin from 52% to 54.5% -- about where the organic business already is. No further acquisitions are assumed, so this is the value of the existing portfolio under the existing playbook.
scenario_narratives.bull: The aftermarket super-cycle runs longer: constrained new-aircraft supply keeps older, parts-hungry fleets flying, OEM build rates finally step up, and defense budgets expand. Organic growth holds 8-10% for four years. Value-based pricing and productivity push margins to 56.5%, and the PMA/DER business acquired with JPE turns from a competitive threat into a growth leg. The upside from continued accretive M&A and levered capital returns is not in the numbers -- it would sit on top of this case.
scenario_narratives.bear: Two things TransDigm is specifically exposed to arrive together: an air-traffic or airline-profitability shock that defers aftermarket spending (FY2020-21 showed revenue can fall 8% and margins 3-4pp), and a harder line on sole-source pricing -- DoD Inspector General cost reviews, legislated cost-data requirements, and airlines turning to PMA parts and used serviceable material. Organic growth is ~1% in year 2 and settles at 3%; margins fall to 50% and only recover to 52% because the newly acquired, lower-margin distribution-style businesses never reach group margins. At 5.7x leverage the equity absorbs all of the EV shortfall, and refinancing the 2028-2030 maturities at higher spreads would cut distributable cash further (not modelled in the unlevered flows; it is the reason for the heavier bear weight).

valuation_philosophy.summary: TransDigm is valued as an unlevered stream of owner free cash flow from its existing portfolio of proprietary, mostly sole-source aerospace components, with the $31.8bn of net debt deducted in full. Leverage is deliberate and serviceable, but it means the equity is a geared claim: small changes in growth, margin or discount rate move the per-share value two to three times as much as they would for an unlevered peer, and the scenario spread and sensitivity grid should be read with that in mind. The model gives no credit for future acquisitions or for the tax-efficient levered capital-return programme beyond what WACC captures.
key_risks_to_valuation: Leverage: 5.7x net debt/EBITDA and ~$1.9bn of annual cash interest; a 10% lower EV is ~15% lower value per share
Pricing power on sole-source parts is the core of the 54% margin and is under recurring DoD Inspector General and congressional scrutiny
Commercial aftermarket is tied to flight hours; FY2020-21 showed the downside
Acquired businesses (JPE/VSA, P&I) entered at roughly half group margin; the base case assumes they are lifted toward it
Year-1 drivers rest on FY2027 guidance taken from the analysis file, not from the earnings release itself
Working-capital intensity (40% of sales) makes FCF conversion sensitive to the growth rate
Total debt definition: Note 10 gross principal used; the MD&A figure is $639M higher (~$11/share)

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (regular-session close); 52-week range 1071.25-1463.03
data_sources.financials: TDG FY2026 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended 2026-09-30): income statement, cash flow statement, Note 10 Debt, EPS note, stock option tables, EBITDA As Defined reconciliation; TDG_Metrics.csv for history
data_sources.qualitative: TDG_Analysis.json (2026-11-15) for FY2027 guidance, bull/bear points and recent developments; FY2026 10-K business, risk factor and MD&A sections

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted, treasury-stock method: 54,589,836 common shares outstanding at 2026-10-30 (FY2026 10-K cover; 54,578,171 at 2026-09-30, so no post-balance-sheet buyback cash is missing from net debt) + ~1.61M net shares from 3.90M options (2014 plan 2,662,535 @ $522.25; 2019 plan 1,241,224 @ $1,131.02, vested and unvested) at the current price. Held FLAT because SBC and dividend-equivalent payments are expensed in the flows. The company's own two-class denominator (57.6M) is a FY2026 weighted average that predates most of the 2.32M shares repurchased in the year and counts vested options gross.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 10-K EBITDA As Defined reconciliation, 'Non-cash stock and deferred compensation expense' $158M (matches the cash-flow add-back), plus $59M of cash dividend-equivalent payments to option holders (financing activities). No net-share-settlement tax line exists: options are exercised for cash ($155M proceeds). Dividend equivalents are lumpy ($208M in FY2025 alongside the $90/share special dividend); the forward path charges ~2.0% of revenue to cover a normalised level.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rates. Cost of equity 10.2% (US 10-year ~4.3% + levered beta ~1.25 x 4.75% ERP). Pre-tax cost of debt 6.2% (10-K: weighted-average cash interest rate on total borrowings), 4.8% after tax at 23%. Capital structure at market: equity ~$68bn, net debt ~$32bn, so ~68/32, giving 8.5%. One WACC across all three scenarios -- risk is charged through the scenario paths and weights, not a second time in the rate. The leverage is carried in the bridge and in WACC, not in the flows: the model's FCF is UNLEVERED (pre-interest), so the ~$1.9bn of annual cash interest is not deducted from flows and the full $31.8bn net debt is deducted from EV.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP. Operating lease cost stays inside EBITDA As Defined and operating lease liabilities are excluded from net debt; finance lease obligations ($344M) are inside total debt and their cost (interest + amortisation) is outside EBITDA. One treatment each, no double count. lease_cost_pct_path therefore omitted.
inputs.nci_treatment: Redeemable NCI $85M + NCI $8M (the ~1-5% minority stubs left in JPE, VSA and P&I) deducted in the equity bridge at book; consolidated flows are 100%. NCI share of income is $1M, immaterial.
inputs.leverage_note: Net debt / FY2026 EBITDA As Defined = 5.7x; stockholders' deficit $(10.0)bn after $90 and $110/share debt-funded special dividends in FY2025 and FY2024. Book equity is meaningless here: equity CAGR, P/B and ROE are not usable. No maintenance covenants outside the revolver; no term-loan or note maturity before August 2028; ~75% of debt fixed or hedged. Equity is a levered stub: at EV ~ $100bn a 10% change in EV moves value per share by ~15%.
inputs.debt_definition_note: total_debt is the Note 10 gross principal ($34,124M incl. $875M securitisation, $344M finance leases, $8M government advances), before $234M of issuance costs and discount. The MD&A liquidity table prints 'Total debt $34,763M', $639M higher, without reconciling the difference; using that figure instead would lower every scenario by ~$11/share.
inputs.last_fcf_basis: last_fcf is the house identity reported FCF (OCF 2,187 - capex 274 = 1,913) - SBC incl. dividend equivalents 217 = 1,696, which is LEVERED (after $1,922M cash interest). The projected flows are unlevered; the comparable FY2026 unlevered owner FCF is ~3,200 (1,696 + 1,922 x (1 - 0.22)).
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component build via Drivers route, 10-year horizon. Routed as a US operating company (dcf-methods routing row 1); the adaptations file was not needed (USD/USD, no material NCI, leases handled as stated). FRESH BUILD -- no prior DCF, no memory entry. Year-1 drivers are anchored to the FY2027 guidance issued 2026-11-10 with Q4 results (net sales $11,950-12,150M, EBITDA As Defined $6,195-6,345M, capex 2.75-3.50% of sales), as recorded in TDG_Analysis.json; the earnings release itself is not in Extracted/. Acquisitions: $4.39bn was spent in FY2026 (Simmonds Oct-2025, JPE/VSA Apr-2026, P&I closed 28-Sep-2026, bolt-ons $434M) and is fully in net debt; the guided FY2027 revenue carries their full-year contribution, so flows and bridge match. No FUTURE acquisitions are modelled: they are assumed value-neutral and funded from the FCF the model treats as distributable. The pending ~$240M Extant product-line purchase (expected FY2027) is excluded from net debt; whether guidance includes its revenue is not known (at most ~0.5% of sales). EBITDA As Defined adds back acquisition/integration costs ($101M in FY2026); with no further deals modelled these are not charged. Buybacks: $2,750M actually repurchased in FY2026 (financing outflow), so the flat count is funded. Management's FY2027 EPS guidance uses 56.7M weighted two-class shares (vested options counted gross); the treasury-stock count used here is 56.2M. The price is a regular-session close.

bear.growth_note: Year 1 = a miss of ~1% against the bottom of the FY2027 guidance range; year 2 carries the downturn.

base.growth_note: Year 1 = FY2027 guidance midpoint (net sales $11,950-12,150M, +14.1%): roughly 7-8% organic plus the full-year carryover of the FY2026 acquisitions. Thereafter organic only, fading from 8% to 4%.
base.margin_note: EBITDA As Defined margin. Year 1 = FY2027 guidance midpoint ($6,195-6,345M, 52.0%). FY2026 was 52.7% consolidated but ~54.6% excluding acquisitions (which earned ~27%: $195M on $725M); the path recovers to 54.5% as acquired units are brought toward group margins.
base.wc_note: Negative: trade working capital (receivables + inventories - payables) is $4.25bn, 40% of sales. All operating asset/liability changes consumed 22%, 58% and 38% of the total revenue increase in FY2024, FY2025 and FY2026 (average ~39%).
base.tax_note: Unlevered cash rate. FY2026 cash taxes $599M plus the ~$460M shield on $2.0bn of interest is ~22% of EBIT; GAAP effective rate 23.7%. No abnormal benefit to ramp out.

bull.growth_note: Year 1 = top of the FY2027 guidance range (+15.1%, 52.2% margin).

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% rather than the house 15%: net debt is 5.7x EBITDA, so a cyclical downturn or a pricing clamp falls on a thin equity layer, and the unlevered flows do not capture higher refinancing costs. It is not higher because there are no maintenance covenants, no maturities before August 2028, ~75% of debt is fixed or hedged, and the business stayed strongly cash-generative through FY2020-21. Base 50%: continuation of a playbook that has delivered for two decades. Bull 30% rather than 35%: it needs both a prolonged aftermarket cycle and further margin expansion from an already exceptional 54-55% organic level.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.

diagnosis.detail: Base year FCF 1,696.0 is 2.1x the historical median 818.5
Structural risks in the qualitative analysis that a standard WACC may not price: customer concentration, cyclicality, regulatory single point of failure
